decision.trend: Research on refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) has been progressing, with a focus on understanding their mechanical properties, such as strength, ductility, and deformation behavior, at elevated temperatures. Earlier studies have investigated the effects of composition, microstructure, and processing on the properties of RHEAs. Recent studies have employed advanced characterization techniques, such as in-situ neutron diffraction and transmission electron microscopy, to elucidate the underlying deformation mechanisms. The trend suggests a growing interest in understanding the relationships between composition, microstructure, and properties in RHEAs, with the goal of developing new materials for high-temperature applications.
